SE-1 (historical-precedent docket, HIGHEST PRIORITY per the report's own sequencing -- 'unblocks everything'): Weberian L/PS derivation-event table, converting registry.py's inert legitimacy/popular_support fields into a specified pipeline. L-channel (traditional/legal-rational): entry oath/privileges confirmed (+1 one-time), charter granted (+1), regular court held (+1 cap), stance-honoring tax collection (0; broken -> -1). PS-channel (charismatic/performance): dearth relieved (+2), festival sponsored (+1), settlement defended (+2), levy taken (-1), forced billeting (-1), public execution of a local (-2). Names the existing SS1.8 Mandate-drift feedback as 'routinization of charisma.' Grounding: Weber 1922 (traditional/legal-rational/charismatic typology maps directly onto the L/PS split); Hirschman 1970 (loyalty as damping). Target: new settlement_layer_v30 SS1.8 subsection. Magnitudes sim-calibrated before ledgering.

SE-2: Dearth chain + granary, replacing settlement_layer SS4.3's one-line famine row. Dearth triggers on entitlement failure (Prosperity 0, grain-route cut per SE-3, or Extraction stance in a Prosperity<=1 settlement), not just weather. Governor response verbs: Open Granary (granary>=1, PS+1 -- Scott 1976 remission), Fix Prices (Order 0, Guild Disposition -1, black-market check -- Thompson 1971 taxation populaire pre-empted), Requisition (displaces dearth to a neighbor), Ignore (Order-2, PS-2, riot targets millers/merchants first per Thompson's documented targeting order). New verb Provision (granary+1, W cost). Grounding: Thompson 1971; Scott 1976; Sen 1981 (entitlement-failure trigger, not availability); Rome's cura annonae; Will & Wong 1991 (Ming-Qing changpingcang granaries). Rides the ED-SE-0001 governance_play_redesign ratification track. SE-3: grain routes -- mechanical teeth for the open geography_v30 item ED-054/BALANCE-005 ('Hafenmark food dependency has no mechanical teeth'). Grounding: Athens' Black Sea grain law; Rome's Egyptian grain fleet; Hanseatic Baltic grain via Danzig; Sen 1981 (siege as entitlement warfare). E-1 — THE BOUND ON THE DEMOGRAPHIC LOOP: matter only, or matter plus hearth capacity? The one question in proposals/2026-09-10-settlements-factions-populations/ that survived all five of CLAUDE.md §0's tests; every other open question in that set was closed with its closing test named (05_COLLISIONS_AND_RESIDUE.md §4). THE CHOICE: P2 ('the bodies clock') as specified is bounded only by the larder — a fed hearth's envelope grows until it cannot feed itself and P1 ('dearth reaches the body') thins it, which is Malthus. THE ALTERNATIVE bounds births additionally by a capacity of the hearth's Sites — a hearth_capacity fixture table per site_kind, adding no new primitive. WHY IT IS NOT AN ENGINEERING CALL: matter-only produces waves the player cannot pre-empt except by holding grain; capacity makes P4 ('found and build') the throttle, which the uploaded nine-game teardown reports as the lever Manor Lords and Banished actually use. Two defensible options, materially different games. LAYER 1 IS SILENT: architecture §25 licenses the clock and names no bound, so §0 test 5 (what makes sense for the architecture) leans matter-only purely because it uses only what exists — which is a cost argument, not a design one. PRICED: matter-only costs nothing new; capacity costs one fixture table and one conjunct in P2's births term. Both ship with P1 as the '−' term either way, so the loop is signed under both arms. SCOPE OF THIS ROW: it queues the question only. description: THE BUILT WORLD -- settlements and their buildings, infrastructure, fortifications and works, as the expression of factions and the contents of their holdings. Document 02 of proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-holdings/. PROPOSED AND HELD BACK IN FULL; nothing ratifies on merge. THE ONTOLOGY: a built thing's FABRIC is a `Site`, its ADDRESS is a `Rung`, and the seam is occupancy, derived rather than stored. This NARROWS ED-IN-0223's *'A BUILDING is a `hearth`'* rather than overturning it -- a building is not a hearth, it STANDS on one, and the hearth is the plot; that is what makes founding expressible and repairs the reading under which a Cathedral had to be a hearth. The licensing argument offered by the design pass (*'breaking a wall would destroy its district'*, via the destroy cascade) WAS FOUND UNSOUND by an antagonist pass -- nothing in the code destroys a Rung or a Site at all -- and the refusal is carried on CARDINALITY instead (holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md S15). Five site families, each discriminated by which EXISTING table its condition band reaches -- PRODUCER, VESSEL, ENCLOSURE, HALL, DWELLING -- under the rule that a kind reaching no new column is not a new family; as roster rows, never carriers. Note `site_kinds` is `[harbour, seam, body]` today and `body` IS NOT A SITE, so the real baseline is two. FORTIFICATION is an ENCLOSURE `Site` whose CONDITION IS ITS STRENGTH -- bands, not a level -- reading onto three mechanisms that already exist (the mass-battle Walls terrain row when intact; a band refusing a `move` on the contain path, which is the chokepoint; a siege as a contest grading a negative condition delta) with NO siege subsystem, and with the epistemic half that an attacker holds only a decaying claim about the band, so it may never be rendered as fact. HOLDINGS: `commit` makes membership, a `hold` on a Rung makes title, `contain` makes presence, and the footing Queries read across them; `serves:` is world-generation content plus a runtime Query over hold-intersect-commit, never a stored fact about a building. `hold` MUST NOT REACH A `Site` -- confirmed, but NOT for the reason proposed: `share` and `draw_share` are declared RESOLVER-SIDE QUERIES (holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md S17), so `share` was never a field and widening `hold` does not make it computable; the ground is that mandatory single-holdership DELETES THE COMMONS, and `share`/`draw_share` being declared-and-unimplemented is the actual `restore` blocker. Because `World.add_tenure` performs no object-class check, that refusal is currently UNENFORCEABLE, so a guard is reported as shipping rather than asked for. THE GHOST POLITY IS LIVE, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: engine/season/harness/populated.py writes 16 `hold` Tenures whose subject is a faction Proposition, which ratified Layer 1 and 01_AXIOMS.md's NEVER-list both forbid -- a Layer 1 / Layer 2 contradiction, fixed by keeping the subject a Person and minting the holders. TWO FREE CUTS WERE WITHDRAWN AS BREAKAGES: `fort_level` has live engine readers behind a BLOCKING descriptor export (engine/autoload/game_state.py declares and DERIVES it from garrison -- *'it is a rule, not data, and authoring it would give one number two owners'* -- and tools/registry.py makes `terr.fort_level` a descriptor key), and `facility_tier` is read live by its own registry and set by its loader. MEASURED THIS SESSION, and it reorders the work: after one season on the populated world 37 settlements hold 4810 units of matter and 211 HEARTHS HOLD NONE -- every site hangs from a settlement, every person lives in a hearth, and the shortfall is clamped away silently. So Jordan's provincial-tax cascade needs the crossing built before a policy can condition anything. MATTER's larder and yield steps ARE built; bodies and travel are not; and matter.py's own `not_implemented` decision row is STALE about larders and yield. RECOMMENDATION ON ED-SE-0051, which stays the open escalation: take the CAPACITY arm, as a `capacity(w, rung)` Query over DWELLING sites with a floor and never a fixture -- the decisive argument being that matter-only is not currently a bound at all, because the shortfall is recorded and not acted on. GRADE: `paper` under CLAUDE.md S0.2.

MATTER AND WORKS -- document 04 of proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-holdings-r2/. PROPOSED, HELD BACK IN FULL. THE MEASURED PROBLEM, reproducible with `python -m engine.season.harness.populated 2`: after one season on build_realm(0), 37 settlements hold 4,810 units of matter and 211 HEARTHS HOLD NONE -- every one of the 74 sites hangs from a settlement, every one of the 46 persons lives in a hearth, and the shortfall is clamped away silently. Worse: only 13 of the 37 settlements have anyone in their contain subtree at all, holding 1,690 of the 4,810, so the other 3,120 sit where nobody lives. MATTER's larder and yield steps ARE built; bodies and travel are not; and matter.py's own `not_implemented` decision row is STALE about larders and yield. THE ANSWER: matter STAYS where it is produced and moves ONLY by `transfer` -- which preserves AX-1, because a person moves it and `transfer` already conserves -- while eaters DRAW UP the ladder through a new `nearest_store(w, rung, kind)` Query, replacing round one's two content moves. Shortfall crosses the gate into `Person.body` (the matrix row exists and gains its writer), bodies cross `band_floors.person` with the same crossing helper as sites, and death at 0 reuses `_eff_kill`'s cascade as `World.remove_person`. `Rung.envelope` is KEPT as ED-SE-0051's carrier. BUILDING is a `works` Record advanced by `work` whose last stage is `restore` or `found` -- and it costs almost nothing new, because `_eff_create_record` ALREADY mints the Record and opens the maker's `hold`, and matter.py's living-holder test already stops a maturation when the maker is gone, so a works that stalls, is inherited, or dies with its master falls out of shipped code. CARRIED FORWARD from round one because it survived a pessimistic pass: the ontology (a built thing's FABRIC is a Site, its ADDRESS is a Rung -- a building stands on a hearth, and the hearth is the plot), the five site families discriminated by which existing table a condition band reaches, fortification as an ENCLOSURE Site whose CONDITION IS ITS STRENGTH with no siege subsystem, and `hold` NOT reaching a Site because mandatory single-holdership deletes the commons. Also carried: the ontology's original licensing argument was found UNSOUND -- nothing in the tree destroys a Rung or a Site -- so it rests on cardinality; and the `fort_level` and `facility_tier` cuts stay WITHDRAWN as breakages, both having live engine readers behind a blocking descriptor export. SCOPED TO POPULATIONS**, per the row's own discharge of `ED-WR-0011`'s pairing rider for NPC generation. SO THE CAPACITY ARM WINS AND THE FIXTURE-TABLE SHAPE LOSES. E-1 asked matter-only (Malthus: a fed hearth's envelope grows until it cannot feed itself, and P1 thins it) against matter plus a bound on the hearth's Sites. The original row proposed that bound as *"a hearth_capacity fixture table per site_kind, adding no new primitive"*; Jordan took the arm and REFUSED that shape -- a QUERY computed from the rung's dwelling Sites, never a table. That distinction is the substance of the ruling, not a detail of it: a fixture table is a second place for a fact the Sites already carry (CLAUDE.md §0.05 cl.1), and it would have made capacity authored rather than derived. WHY THE FOUR SURFACES DISAGREED, recorded so the shape is recognisable next time. The RULINGS sheet said `ruled`; this ledger said `open`/`needs_jordan: true`; `HANDOFF_SE.md` said *"STAYS OPEN"* in three places; and the r2 documents said the capacity arm was *"recommended, not adopted"*. Jordan ruled on 2026-09-18 (`ED-IN-0255`) that subsistence is TERRITORIAL -- *"it's a territorial issue"*, with NPC synecdoches for the affected population. A capacity bound scoped to POPULATIONS and computed per rung is consistent with that and is the same scale; the two rulings are read together, and neither is a per-person body quantity. `ED-IN-0247`'s `body_step` remains the open scale question, unchanged here.
